summary: Silent snapshotter process reserving GPU slots and causing autoscaler sensor misclassification leading to dedicated throughput collapse
description:
Issue summary:
At ~2026-03-12 10:40 UTC DataSage (dedicated pool) reported sudden p50/p99 throughput collapse for batched routes. No standard autoscaler events or capacity shortages were shown in high-level dashboards. Investigation found a background snapshotter process holding ephemeral GPU reservations (not visible in normal slot metrics) and producing heartbeat jitter that the autoscaler sensor interpreted as a large increase in small-streams, triggering conservative shrink decisions and preventing new attachments.

Impact:
- Customer: DataSage Analytics (dedicated) experienced ~60% drop in sustained throughput across pinned batched routes for ~45 minutes.
- Business: SLA blips for the customer during peak processing window.

Timeline (brief):
- 10:38 UTC: Monitoring alert p99 throughput up > 2x for DataSage reserved pool.
- 10:40 UTC: Customer opened support channel and ticket (this issue).
- 10:45 UTC: Support triaged to SRE; initial telemetry collected.
- 10:55 UTC: SRE observed slot attach backlog and autoscaler downscale triggers.
- 11:10 UTC: Identified snapshotter snapshots running concurrently on GPUs; manual restart of snapshotter replica started at 11:18 UTC.
- 11:25 UTC: Throughput recovered to baseline by 11:30 UTC; ticket escalated to eng for fix.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ds-data-prod-usw1
- Region: us-west
- Runtime image: rw-infer-2026-02-26
- Autoscaler sensor window configuration: 30s sample / 3-min smoothing

Steps to reproduce (repro is non-trivial; approximated):
1) Provision a dedicated pool with a background snapshotter configured to write incremental checkpoints every ~2 minutes.
2) Generate a mix of long-batched requests and many small short streams from a synthetic tenant.
3) Trigger concurrent snapshot compaction (simulate snapshotter scanning incremental checkpoints).
4) Observe slot attach latencies, autoscaler downscale events and throughput drop.

Observed logs & metrics excerpts:
- serving-runtime logs: "attach_delay_ms=1250 slot_reserve_attempts=3" repeated across hosts.
- snapshotter logs: "Compacting checkpoint shard: gpu0 shard_id=17 reserved_fd=1" (multiple hosts)
- autoscaler telemetry: downscale_decision{window=180s} -> aggressive_shrink due to perceived small-stream fraction rising from 0.12 -> 0.47 in 2 minutes.
- NVMe/IO metrics: short I/O latency spikes (p99 IO latency increased 3x during compaction windows).

Business/Customer notes:
Customer observed backlog of queued requests in their application and reported higher retry rates. DataSage is mid-enterprise and depends on predictable reserved throughput during daily processing windows.

2026-03-12 10:51 - SRE (Marco): Observed attach backlog and autoscaler downscale traces. Collecting diag bundles from ds-data-prod-usw1 hosts. Punting to infra-engineer for snapshotter correlation.

2026-03-12 11:06 - Infra (Lina Gomez): Snapshotter compaction jobs found running on 6/8 GPUs in pool; compaction holds temporary file descriptors and pins GPU memory briefly. Scheduled manual restart of snapshotter replica to confirm impact.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Snapshotter compaction holds ephemeral GPU reservations + generates IO bursts leading to attach latencies and autoscaler mis-reading small-stream fraction.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler sensor window too narrow combined with IO-induced attach jitter caused aggressive shrink decisions instead of transient stabilization.

Evidence: Correlated timestamps between snapshotter compaction log entries and autoscaler downscale events across 6 hosts. IO p99 spikes coincident with attach_delay_ms spikes. No driver or hardware errors present.
Repro attempt: Local repro with injected IO compaction on small test pool reproduced autoscaler reacting within the configured window; increasing autoscaler smoothing prevents premature shrink.
Short-term mitigation tested: Restart snapshotter replica -> immediate drop in attach delays and autoscaler stabilized; validated by customer during recovery window.
resolution:
Root cause: Snapshotter compaction jobs on tenant-dedicated hosts were performing concurrent checkpoint compactions that temporarily pinned GPU resources via ephemeral reservations and produced short NVMe IO pressure. The autoscaler’s small-stream fraction sensor and smoothing window interpreted attach jitter as a shift toward many short streams and made conservative downscale decisions, preventing new attachments and reducing throughput.

Fixes implemented:
- Infra PR #4578: add compaction backpressure limiter to snapshotter (limits concurrent compactions per host) and make compaction IO more rate-limited.
- Autoscaler config change: increase smoothing window from 3m to 5m for dedicated pools and add a guard to ignore single-window spikes when attach_delay_ms > 800ms but without slot-free events.
- Monitoring: New alert created for "snapshotter_compaction_rate" and "attach_delay_ms" correlation; dashboard panel added to dedicated pool runbook.

Rollout & follow-up:
- PR merged 2026-03-12; staged canary deployed to staging cluster 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC; no regressions observed.
- Production rollout scheduled in two phases: low-traffic pools then full rollout (completed 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC).
- Postmortem: schedule follow-up with DataSage to review SLAs and offer 10% credit for the impacted window.
- Owner for permanence: Marco Lin (infra) to track post-deploy metrics for 7 days and close monitoring with CS.
